newsitem.title: BRAZIL: South American port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: South American port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

BRAZIL, Oct 1, Vitoria - vessels berthed 3 general cargo loaders/dischargers, 1 sugar loader, 1 store, 2 wheat dischargers, 1 pig iron loader. Tubarao 3 iron ore loaders, 1 petroleum. Praia Mole 3 steel plates loaders, 2 bulk coal dischargers. Portocel 1 cellulose loader. Ubu 2 iron ore loaders. 25 vessels waiting in roads. Santos -vessels berthed 10 full containers, 5 general cargo, 1 bulk cement discharger, 14 sugar loaders, 1 chemical discharger, 1 wheat discharger, 3 fertiliser dischargers, 1 pellets loader, 1 salt discharger, 1 fruit loader, 1 container/general cargo discharger, 1 sulphur discharger, 1 diesel loader, 1 propane discharger. 90 vessels waiting in roads, 40 due in next 7 days. Private terminals Cosipa 3 steel products loaders, 1 iron ore, 1 bulk coal discharger. Ultrafertil 1 bulk sulphur discharger. Rio Grande - vessels berthed 3 bulk fertiliser dischargers, 2 containers, 5 soy loaders, 2 waiting in roads, 25 due during next 10 days. Sao Sebastiao - vessels berthed Tebar 4 vessels. Five waiting in roads, 4 due during next 7 day. Rio de Janeiro - vessels berthed 2 general cargo/steel dischargers, 1 wheat discharger, 4 general cargo dischargers, 1 caustic soda discharger, 2 sugar loaders, 1 steel products loader, 1 general loader. Tecon 2 vessels. 27 vessels due in next 7 days. Itajai - vessels berthed 1 general cargo, 2 reefers, 2 full containers, 12 in roads, 14 due in next 7 days.

EL SALVADOR, Sept 26 - Acajutla - 14 vessels due for discharging (petroleum, steel products, sulphate, containers, corn, grease and sunflower oil, vehicles, diesel oil, bulk corn, general cargo and containers). No delays expected. 1 vessel discharging rice at berth.

HONDURAS, Puerto Cortes - Sept 30 - Three vessels berthed of which 1 discharging soy, 2 loading bananas, 2 anchored of which 1 to discharge/load containers, 1 to load bananas. 12 due of which 8 to discharge/load containers, 3 to load bananas, 1 to load concentrates. No berthing delays expected. Vessels berthed 2 discharging/loading containers, 1 discharging soymeal in bulk, 1 loading bananas, 1 loading bananas/discharging containers. Vessels waiting 6 to discharge/load containers, 2 to discharge bananas, 1 steel, 1 to load containers/discharge lead. Vessels due 2 to discharge/load containers, 4 to discharge/load general, 3 to load bananas, 1 to discharge paper, 1 corn, 1 mill feed.

PERU, Sept 30 - Callao - Six vessels in bay, 8 in pier (general cargo/containers), no delays. Ita - two vessels in pier (general cargo/bulk wheat), no delays. Bayovar, Pisco - no vessels. Talara - one oil vessel in pier, no delays. Chimbote - two vessels in bay, 1 in pier (fishmeal), no delays. Ilo - one copper vessel in pier, no delays.

VENEZUELA, Sept 30 - Puerto Cabello - three vessels anchored, 6 berthed of which 3 grain, 2 general cargo, 1 container vessel. Piers 1 and 2 closed. Guanta - four anchored, 3 general cargo berthed. Oct 1 - Orinoco river draft 37 ft 6 in. Puerto Ordaz - one loading iron ore, 5 vessels due. Boca Grande - one loading iron ore, 2 due. Mile 178 - six at anchorage to load/discharge. Matanzas - two at anchorage to load, 6 operating of which 5 loading steel products, 1 discharging scrap, 5 due. Venalum - one loading aluminium, 1 due. San Felix - one loading iron ore. Punta cuchillo - one due. Puerto Cabello 10 operating of which 8 loading/discharging generals, 2 discharging grain, 8 due. Maracaibo - four loading/discharging generals. Bajo Grande - one loading refined products, 1 due. Buoy b71 - one due. Puerto Miranda four loading crude. El Tablazo - one loading urea, 1 due. San Francisco - one loading crude. Palmarejo Sur, La Salina, Punta Camacho, La Ceiba - no vessels. Guanta - two operating of which 1 discharging wheat, 1 loading generals, 2 due. Amuay - no data. La Guaira - three loading/discharging generals, 4 due, 3 under repairs. All ports working normally.
